question: Under EU Schengen rules, how many days may a visa-exempt non-EU short-stay visitor spend in the Schengen area within any 180-day period?
answer: A visa-exempt non-EU short-stay visitor may spend a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area. [2][4][6] The 90 days are calculated as a single period across all the European countries using the EES, not per country. [2] The UK government's France advice (dated 8 November 2026) adds that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days, and that overstaying can lead to a ban of up to 3 years for UK travellers. [3] Since 10 April 2026 the EES has been fully operational and records entry and exit dates, and it identifies overstayers. [2]

keyPoints.text: Visa-exempt non-EU nationals may stay a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area.
The 90-day limit is calculated as a single period across all EES-using Schengen countries, not per country.
Visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before travel count towards the 90-day limit.
Overstaying the 90-day limit can result in a ban from entering Schengen countries for up to 3 years.
The EES checks the 90/180-day rule electronically and records overstays, replacing passport stamping from 10 April 2026.

mayBeStale.text: Source 5 says EES started on 12 October 2025, while Source 2 says full operation began 10 April 2026 after a six-month phased rollout; the start-date framing differs.
Source 2 is undated and Source 6 and 7 are partial search snippets, so their details may not reflect current rules.
Source 4 is dated 2019 in metadata despite containing 2026 content, so its date stamp is unreliable.
